title: Text Is All You Need: Learning Language Representations for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Sequential recommendation must model dynamic user behavior from historical interactions to understand user preferences.

gap.claim: Existing approaches struggle to model cold-start items and transfer knowledge to new datasets.

contributions.claim: Recformer models user preferences and item features as language representations intended to generalize to new items and datasets.
The framework represents each item as a sentence formed by flattening textual key-value attributes, turning a user's item sequence into a sequence of sentences.

Recformer uses a Longformer-like bidirectional Transformer with different embedding layers for sequential recommendation, together with pretraining and finetuning methods that combine language understanding and recommendation tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Recformer as a novel framework and identify the pretraining and finetuning methods as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on six datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of Recformer for sequential recommendation.
The reported effectiveness is especially strong in low-resource and cold-start settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation models dynamic user behavior and preferences from interaction histories.
Existing item-ID and textual-feature approaches have difficulty with cold-start items and transfer to new datasets.
Recformer represents item attributes and item sequences as language-like sentences and learns to retrieve the next sentence.
The framework uses a Longformer-like bidirectional Transformer and task-combining pretraining and finetuning methods.
The authors report effectiveness across six datasets, particularly in low-resource and cold-start settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the six datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the pretraining and finetuning procedures in detail.
The abstract does not establish performance outside the reported low-resource and cold-start settings.
